moves.headline: Perkins brings new 2606 (13 L) and 5012 (46 L) engines to Middle East Energy 2025 in Dubai
moves.summary: Perkins showcased the 2606 (350 to 550 kVA at 50 Hz, available H2 2025, 1,000 hour service intervals, HVO and B100 capable) and the electronic 5012 (1,275 to 1,875 kVA at 50 Hz, 1,125 to 1,500 kWe at 60 Hz, ISO G3, NFPA110, EPA Tier 2 on 60 Hz). Applications cited: data centres, hospitals, power plants.
moves.analysis: The 5012 sits exactly on the 1,250 to 1,875 kVA band where Cummins Arabia sells QSK50 and QSK60 based sets into data centres and hospitals, and it is offered to every independent packager in the Gulf. The 2606 attacks the 350 to 550 kVA band with 1,000 hour service intervals. Cummins Arabia should benchmark total cost of ownership against 5012-powered Jubaili and Teksan sets and lead with factory-packaged reliability, local service coverage and 50 degree C ambient performance.

moves.headline: Perkins shows 2600 Series, hydrogen hybrid IOPU and battery-electric power unit at CONEXPO 2026
moves.summary: Perkins announced the 904J-E36TTA (129 kW), the 13 litre 2600 Series (340 to 515 kW, Stage V and Tier 4 Final), Project Coeus hydrogen hybrid IOPU (379 kW combined) and a 95.5 kW battery-electric power unit. Richard Hemmings, VP and GM Global Sales, Marketing, Service and Parts, framed the message as lower total cost of ownership and future fuel readiness.
moves.analysis: Hybrid and alternative fuel work is still at prototype stage for Perkins and is aimed at off-highway more than gensets. The relevant signal is the Stage V 2600 Series, which packagers can pair with Gulf tenders that start asking for Stage V or Tier 4 Final in urban and data centre sites. Cummins Arabia should keep its own Stage V and Tier 4 Final genset offer visible to consultants in UAE and KSA.

moves.headline: FG Wilson gensets pass HVO field trials with Tria Energy
moves.summary: FG Wilson Engineering (Dublin) Ltd and Tria Energy reported diesel-equivalent performance on HVO (EN 15940) across load conditions with no engine or fuel system changes, up to 90 percent lifecycle CO2 savings, aimed at data centre, construction and critical infrastructure customers.
moves.analysis: HVO acceptance is becoming a standard question in data centre tenders in the UAE. FG Wilson now has published trial evidence to cite. Cummins Arabia should have equivalent HVO approval statements for its data centre range ready in tender documents.

moves.headline: FG Wilson Catalyst 2026: 60th anniversary global dealer conference in Belfast
moves.summary: FG Wilson gathered its global dealer network, customers and staff in Belfast's Titanic Quarter for a week of strategy, innovation and growth sessions and a Product Discovery Zone. No new product launches were announced.
moves.analysis: A dealer conference of this scale signals a channel re-energising exercise. Expect dealer targets and campaign activity in the Gulf over the next 12 months, especially from FG Wilson (Engineering) FZE and TAMGO. Cummins Arabia should expect sharper FG Wilson pricing in the 500 to 1,500 kVA commercial band.

moves.headline: FG Wilson appoints Roger Kennedy as General Manager
moves.summary: Roger Kennedy, a 30 year FG Wilson veteran with a commercial background, was appointed General Manager to lead the FG Wilson team worldwide.
moves.analysis: A commercially oriented GM tends to prioritise dealer growth and volume. Combined with the Catalyst 2026 conference, this points to a growth push rather than a hold strategy for FG Wilson.
moves.date_note: Undated on fgwilson.com; listed among current top stories

moves.headline: FG Wilson lists new 'M' variants across the large range (P1100-1M to P2500-3M) with DSE7410 control
moves.summary: FG Wilson's large range pages now pair each legacy model with an M variant (P1100-1M, P1650-1M, P2250-3M, P2500-3M), all on Perkins 4008, 4012 and 4016 engines, FG Wilson alternators with AREP excitation and Deep Sea 7410 controllers, with new datasheets dated 2024-10 and 2026-03.
moves.analysis: FG Wilson's top end remains 2,500 kVA on the mechanical 4016-61TRG3 while the electronic 5016 is sold to other packagers. Cummins Arabia's C2500 to C3500 range and its factory data centre ratings remain a differentiator above 2,500 kVA and in DCC rated applications. Below 2,500 kVA expect the refreshed FG Wilson range to be pushed hard by TAMGO and FG Wilson FZE.
moves.date_note: Date taken from the Caterpillar media asset ID of the P2500-3M datasheet (CM20260306)

moves.headline: Generac standardises 1,000 to 1,500 kW US industrial diesel sets on Perkins 4008 (30.6 L) and 4012/D46L (45.8 L) engines
moves.summary: Generac's SD1000/MD1000 use the Perkins 30.6 L 8 cylinder engine and the SD1250/MD1250 (1,250 and 1,500 kW nodes) use the Perkins D46L 12 cylinder engine with Deep Sea G8601 controllers.
moves.analysis: Perkins gains a large 60 Hz OEM volume base through Generac, which feeds 60 Hz product maturity relevant to Saudi Arabia. If Generac's Gulf dealers (Atlas Power Solutions, Watan Altaqa, Al Mulla) bring these sets to KSA, Cummins Arabia faces Perkins-powered 1,000 to 1,500 kW packages under a second brand.
moves.date_note: Date from Generac D46L sell sheet version 1125

moves.headline: Jubaili Bros (Perkins packager) signs strategic partnership with Wholesale Electric Asia for oil and gas power packages
moves.summary: Jubaili Bros (1,600 employees, 11 countries, 3 manufacturing plants, 1.5 GW annual capacity) and Singapore based WEA agreed to cooperate on power generation distribution and customised oil and gas packages across the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia.
moves.analysis: Jubaili Bros is scaling as a regional packager and now targets oil and gas packages, a core Cummins Arabia segment in KSA and Kuwait. Its Perkins-based JP range runs to 2,250 kVA prime. Cummins Arabia should monitor Jubaili's Saudi factory ramp and its bids into Aramco contractor and rental fleets.

moves.headline: Jubaili Bros adds MWM gas gensets (400 to 4,500 kW) for Middle East and Africa
moves.summary: MWM (Mannheim) and Jubaili Bros (Dubai) announced a partnership to offer MWM gas generators of 400 to 4,500 kW electrical across MEA, under Group CEO Dr Marcus Schumacher.
moves.analysis: This is context for the Perkins channel: Jubaili now covers diesel (Perkins) and gas (MWM), which lets it bid full gas and diesel packages against Cummins Arabia's HSK78G and diesel range. Included as a late 2024 baseline because it shapes 2025 to 2026 bidding behaviour.

Mid-range diesel sets (SD1000, SD1250) use Perkins 4008 and 4012 engines, and its own spark-ignited gas engines power the SG/MG range to 1,000 kW

moves.headline: Generac Q1 2026: C&I sales up 28 percent on data centre demand; final-stage vendor approval with multiple hyperscalers
moves.summary: Net sales rose 12 percent to US$1.06 billion, C&I external sales rose about 28 percent to US$510 million, and Generac raised full-year guidance to mid-to-high teens growth with C&I in the mid-to-high 20s percent.
moves.analysis: Confirms Generac is becoming a scale supplier of large data centre gensets. For Cummins Arabia this is a new name on hyperscaler approved vendor lists rather than an immediate local competitor.

moves.headline: Generac signs global supply agreement with a hyperscale data centre operator covering APAC, Europe, Middle East and Latin America
moves.summary: The unnamed hyperscaler qualified Generac after factory visits and performance reviews. Production is at Beaver Dam, Oshkosh and Sussex, Wisconsin. Generac cited its EPC Power collaboration and Enercon enclosure acquisition.
moves.analysis: The Middle East is explicitly in scope, so Gulf hyperscale sites can be supplied from a global frame agreement without a local tender. Cummins Arabia should coordinate with Cummins Inc. global hyperscale account teams to defend Saudi and UAE campuses and make sure local service capability is part of the global pitch.

moves.headline: Generac SD3250 (3.25 MW, Baudouin Baudouin M55) wins Consulting-Specifying Engineer 2026 gold award; large diesel series 1.75 to 3.25 MW
moves.summary: The 3.25 MW unit is Generac's largest diesel set, part of a new large diesel series from 1.75 to 3.25 MW built for data centres, healthcare and infrastructure.
moves.analysis: The series maps onto Cummins Arabia's C2000 to C3500 data centre band. Note the engine is Baudouin, so the product competes on Generac packaging and Baudouin lead time, not on a proprietary engine.

moves.headline: Generac buys Belvidere, Illinois plant to add large-megawatt genset packaging capacity from Q1 2027, after February 2026 Enercon acquisition
moves.summary: The facility adds over 100 jobs and follows the acquisition of Enercon Engineering (enclosures and switchgear) and expansions in Oshkosh, Beaver Dam and Sussex.
moves.analysis: More US packaging capacity shortens Generac lead times for export orders in 2027. Cummins Arabia should expect Generac to quote competitive delivery on Gulf hyperscale sites from 2027.

moves.headline: Generac promotes Niccolo Borracchini to EVP International (Generac and Pramac outside US and Canada)
moves.summary: Borracchini, with Pramac since 2015 and SVP International since 2024, now leads EMEA, APAC and LATAM; Paolo Campinoti retired 2026-07-01 to an advisory role.
moves.analysis: A Pramac-rooted leader running international suggests the Gulf will be served through the Pramac Dubai structure. Cummins Arabia should track whether PR Middle East FZE begins quoting large Generac data centre sets in UAE and KSA.

moves.headline: Generac Q2 2026: data centre backlog about US$1.6 billion, second hyperscale agreement secured, C&I up 29 percent
moves.summary: Net sales US$1.17 billion (up 11 percent); C&I US$556 million; nearly US$700 million committed for 2027 from the first hyperscale agreement and about US$1 billion of additional orders; full-year C&I growth guided to the low 30s percent.
moves.analysis: Two hyperscale frame agreements in one quarter means Generac is now a standing option for hyperscaler standby fleets. Cummins Arabia's exposure is in Saudi and UAE hyperscale campuses awarded through global procurement.

The 73.2 MW Saudi hyperscale delivery and the first EMEIA BESS commissioning in Dubai are its current reference points

moves.headline: Cummins Arabia completes DMC6000 master controller retrofit for a Riyadh telecom operator
moves.summary: Three 800 kW QSK23-G3 gensets at a major network and communication service provider in Riyadh moved from a 20 year old MC-150 master controller to a PowerCommand DMC6000 with PCC3300 upgrades, completed in a six week shutdown window under Cummins Arabia supervision.
moves.analysis: Installed-base modernisation is a repeatable revenue line in KSA telecom and data centre sites running legacy PowerCommand controls. Cummins Arabia can package DMC6000 retrofits with service contracts as a defensive move against competitor replacement offers.

moves.headline: Cummins launches containerised BESS in the UAE through Cummins Arabia
moves.summary: Cummins Power Generation, Cummins Arabia and Cummins Middle East launched the LFP battery energy storage range in Dubai, with Amit Deshpande (Managing Director) and Emad Lotfy (Power Generation Business Director) quoted. Cummins Arabia was described as 550 plus staff, 10 service branches, 8 warehouses, an HHP Master Rebuild Center and a training centre across UAE, KSA and Kuwait.
moves.analysis: Gives Cummins Arabia a hybrid genset plus storage offer for rental, data centre and oil and gas customers before most genset competitors in the Gulf have a factory-branded BESS with genset controller integration. The 50 Hz only listing means KSA 60 Hz sites need confirmation of a 60 Hz variant.

moves.headline: Cummins Arabia publishes 73.2 MW Saudi hyperscale data centre reference
moves.summary: Thirty DQLC and six DQCA enclosed gensets (36 units, 73.2 MW) were delivered in seven months to a regional technology provider's hyperscale sites across Saudi Arabia, engineered for 50 C ambient with remote radiators, dual ACB panels, Ni-Cad batteries and fuel coolers, tested to Uptime Institute requirements.
moves.analysis: This is the proof point for 60 Hz QSK78 supply into KSA hyperscale programmes. The case study states the customer recommended Cummins Arabia for future phases, so follow-on capacity should be protected with reserved production slots given Cummins Inc reports record data centre order books.

moves.headline: Cummins announces S17 Centum 17 litre genset up to 1000 kW
moves.summary: New S17 engine based Centum Series (C600D6E to C1000D6ED, 60 Hz, EPA Tier 2 stationary emergency) with 25,000 plus hours of validation and a three year base warranty, aimed at commercial, healthcare and water treatment standby.
moves.analysis: A 1 MW class set on a 17 L block cuts footprint and fuel against 23 L to 30 L competitors in the 600 to 1000 kW band that dominates KSA hospital, commercial and telecom tenders. Cummins Arabia should confirm 60 Hz availability for Africa Middle East and price it against Cat C18 and mtu 12V1600 class units.

moves.headline: Cummins reports FY2025 revenue of USD 33.7 billion; Power Systems sales USD 7.46 billion
moves.summary: Full year 2025 revenue USD 33.7 billion (down 1 percent), net income USD 2.8 billion, EBITDA USD 5.4 billion. Power Systems segment sales USD 7.463 billion with EBITDA USD 1.694 billion (22.7 percent); Q4 Power Systems sales up 11 percent on data centre demand in North America, China and Asia Pacific.
moves.analysis: Power Systems is the growth engine of the parent, but the cited demand regions do not include the Middle East. Cummins Arabia competes internally for HHP allocation; documented Gulf pipeline visibility is what secures slots against North American and Asian data centre orders.

moves.headline: First Cummins BESS in EMEIA commissioned at Cummins Arabia Al Quoz, Dubai
moves.summary: A C400B5ZE (422 kWh / 200 kW) was commissioned in Q3 2025 at Cummins Arabia's Al Quoz facility for peak shaving alongside containerised diesel gensets; Q4 2025 results were 12.7 MWh discharged, 382 generator hours and 5,443.5 litres of diesel avoided.
moves.analysis: A live, metered hybrid reference on Cummins Arabia's own site is the demonstration asset for rental fleets, remote oil and gas camps and construction sites in the UAE and KSA. The measured fuel and runtime savings give the sales team quantified payback material.

moves.headline: Cummins raises 2030 targets and announces large-engine capacity and product investments at Analyst Day
moves.summary: At its 2026 Analyst Day Cummins raised 2030 financial targets and announced further capacity and product investments to strengthen positioning in mining and power generation; Power Systems President Jenny Bush said demand for reliable power is accelerating at an unprecedented pace. Dollar and GW figures are in the presentation, not the release.
moves.analysis: Added HHP capacity is the constraint that decides whether Cummins Arabia can bid multi-hundred megawatt KSA data centre phases on schedule. Cummins Arabia should lock forward allocation agreements for QSK78 and QSK95 sets while capacity ramps.

moves.headline: Cummins to supply HSK78G and QSK60 gas gensets for Circe Energy HPC data centres in West Texas
moves.summary: Behind-the-meter prime power natural gas microgrids for AI and HPC data centres using HSK78G (C2000N6CD) and QSK60 (C1400N6) gensets, deliveries 2026 to 2030 with modular deployment from 2027.
moves.analysis: Gas prime power for data centres is now a Cummins reference model. In KSA and the UAE, where pipeline gas is available at industrial sites, Cummins Arabia can propose HSK78G prime power or bridging power for data centre and industrial loads waiting on grid connections.

moves.headline: Cummins introduces QSK78 Centum Series to the 50 Hz market
moves.summary: New 50 Hz HHP Centum gensets on the QSK78 platform, up to 3500 kVA standby and 3300 kVA continuous for data centres, with PowerCommand 3400, Centum Transmission Drive, Tier 2 and Low NOx options and HVO compatibility, announced from Daventry, UK for Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia Pacific and Latin America.
moves.analysis: Extends the data-centre-optimised Centum footprint to the 50 Hz UAE and Kuwait markets where the C2750D5 and C3000D5 previously carried the QSK78 range. Cummins Arabia should obtain the model data sheets and position the 3300 kVA continuous rating against Cat 3516E and mtu 20V4000 offers in UAE hyperscale tenders.

moves.headline: Cummins Q2 2026: Power Systems sales up 19 percent to USD 2.3 billion, outlook raised
moves.summary: Q2 2026 revenue USD 9.5 billion (up 9 percent), net income USD 932 million, EBITDA 17.5 percent. Power Systems sales USD 2.3 billion (up 19 percent) with EBITDA USD 552 million (24.5 percent) on robust data centre standby orders; full year revenue growth guidance raised to 10 to 13 percent.
moves.analysis: Strong global order intake tightens HHP lead times and pricing power for the parent. For Cummins Arabia the implication is lead time discipline in Gulf bids and early engagement with consultants so that Saudi and UAE projects are in the order book before slots fill.

moves.headline: Cummins wins 5 MWh BESS supply for a large US data centre
moves.summary: Cummins selected to supply LFP battery energy storage systems with 5 MWh nominal capacity for a large US data centre project, its largest BESS deployment to date, to manage AI-driven load fluctuations and support utility interconnection requirements.
moves.analysis: Validates BESS as a data centre product line, not only a remote-power line. Cummins Arabia can bundle BESS with genset blocks in KSA and UAE data centre proposals to address load-following and interconnection ramp requirements.

moves.headline: HSK78G certified for hydraulic fracturing (EPA Tier 2 mobile off-highway)
moves.summary: The 78 litre, 12 cylinder HSK78G natural gas engine, rated 3000 bhp, received EPA Tier 2 large spark-ignition mobile off-highway certification for well servicing, joining the Spark-Ignited Pumping Power portfolio.
moves.analysis: Relevant to Cummins Arabia's oil and gas engine business as Saudi unconventional gas programmes expand; also confirms the HSK78G platform's power density that underpins the C2000N gas genset range offered in the Gulf.

Cummins Arabia.company_size: Over 550 professionals (Cummins press release, April 2025); close to 500 employees of 30 plus nationalities at launch (June 2017)
Cummins Arabia.strategic_positioning: Cummins Arabia is the exclusive Cummins distribution and service JV for Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait, formed in 2017 by Cummins Inc. and Olayan, whose Cummins distribution history in Saudi Arabia dates to 1956. It runs 10 service branches, 8 warehouses, an HHP Master Rebuild Center and a service training centre with 550 plus staff. Its competitive position in Gulf power generation rests on the Cummins HHP range (QSK60, QSK78, QSK95 and the new Centum Series) for 60 Hz Saudi and 50 Hz UAE and Kuwait data centres, the PowerCommand controls and DMC paralleling family, and the 2025 addition of factory BESS. The 73.2 MW Saudi hyperscale delivery and the first EMEIA BESS commissioning in Dubai are its current reference points

tenders.leanTxt:
WHAT IT IS
Phase Two of the Royal Saudi Air Force's King Saud Air Base (383 sq km, Hafr Al-Batin, Eastern Region). Owner: Ministry of Defence (RSAF is named as the government entity on Etimad). MEED (10 Sep 2026): 'Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defence & Aviation has started the tendering process for the next phase of the King Saud Air Base in the kingdom. Contractors have been given until 20 October to submit their bids. The scope of works covers the construction of the headquarters building, administrative buildings, operations and maintenance area, police camp facilities, weapons and ammunition area, residential facilities, airfield facilities and other associated facilities. The project duration is three years.' (https://guest.meed.com/saudi-arabia-tenders-next-phase-of-king-saud-air-base/). Construction Review Online (10 Sep 2026) adds that the tender follows 'an earlier qualification process for the design and construction of Phase Two facilities' and that the qualification scope 'also included power generation, water and wastewater pumping stations, and fiber-optic communications'. It gives qualification ref. 241140017394 and names Dar AlRiyadh as project consultant (https://constructionreviewonline.com/king-saud-air-base-1-36-billion-phase-two-construction-tender-moves-saudi-project-forward/). The base was launched in March 2016 (foundation stone laid by King Salman) as a three-phase redevelopment of the former advanced air base (SPA, https://www.spa.gov.sa/1475763). An earlier master plan by Stanley Consultants, for client USACE Middle East District, notes the base 'needed extensive utility infrastructure such as power plants, pumping stations, roads, water and sewer' (https://www.stanleyconsultants.com/solutions/planning-consulting/project/king-saud-air-base).

PHASE ONE / SISTER PACKAGES (who holds the power scope today)
- Phase One: about SR6.6bn ($1.8bn), awarded 'early last year' (i.e. early 2025). Package 1 (~SR2.9bn/$783m) went to a JV of Isam Khairi Kabbani Group and Alfanar Projects. Package 2 (~$1bn) went to Albawani, Shibh Al-Jazira Contracting and Kuwait's Alghanim International (MEED, same url).
- Petrojet (Egypt) won a SAR600m ($160m) contract in Sept 2025 for 'civil works at King Saud Air Base ... connections, protection, and electrical networks, as well as sewage and water lines linked to a power plant'. The work is in partnership with Alfanar and Isam Khairi Kabbani Group, with an 18-month completion (Mubasher, 14 Sep 2025, https://en.sharikatmubasher.com/media-hub/news/21506235/egypts-petrojet-wins-160mn-contract-in-saudi-arabia?lang=en). So a base power plant already sits in the Phase One Kabbani/Alfanar scope. The genset or engine brand of that plant is NOT public. Whether it is diesel, gas or grid-backed is also not public.
- MEP subcontractors and genset brands on Phase One: not found in any public source (checked MEED guest API, Construction Review, Mubasher, web search in English and Arabic).

SCOPE & RATINGS
- Public sources give no genset schedule, count or kVA. The qualification scope lists 'power generation' plus water and wastewater pumping stations. From that (INFERENCE), the Phase Two contractor supplies (a) generation or standby for the new HQ/admin, O&M, police camp, weapons and ammunition and residential zones, and (b) standby at each pumping station, tied into the Phase One power plant and networks.
- Frequency: Saudi Arabia is 60 Hz (230/400 V LV). Sets must therefore be the 60 Hz range (Cummins 'D6' models, e.g. C2000D6 = 2,000 kWe standby / 1,825 kWe prime on QSK60), NOT the D5 (50 Hz) models listed in the earlier record.
- Site conditions (INFERENCE): Hafr Al-Batin summer ambient reaches about 50 C, so specs will call for high-ambient cooling (50-55 C) and derated outputs, plus desert filtration.
- Standards (INFERENCE, not confirmed): the MoD/RSAF MEP spec for this package is not public. Historic RSAF bases were planned under USACE (per Stanley), so specs may cite US/NFPA practice (NFPA 110 Level 1 for life-safety/critical, UFC-style prime/standby definitions) alongside SBC 401 (IEC-based). Ask Dar AlRiyadh which spec book applies.

DATES & PROCESS
- Qualification (Etimad ref. 241140017394) completed earlier. The bid is restricted to qualified firms.
- Bid submission: 20 Oct 2026 (MEED). No extension reported as of 29 Sep 2026.
- Contract: design-and-build, 3 years.
- Tender number, document fee, site-visit and pre-bid dates are not public (Etimad restricted).

COMMERCIAL TERMS (general Saudi rules, not tender-specific)
- Saudi Government Tenders & Procurement Law norms: initial (bid) guarantee typically 1-2% of bid value and final (performance) guarantee 5%. NOT verified for this tender.
- LCGPA local content: a price preference for local products and a mandatory list apply to government purchases. Whether diesel gensets are on the current LCGPA Mandatory List is NOT confirmed (searches found tiles, pumps, valves, cables and split ACs, not gensets). Either way, a local-content certificate score and local packaging help in evaluation. From 1 Aug 2026, mandatory-list items also need a minimum enterprise local-content score (SPA, https://www.spa.gov.sa/en/N2514218).

ELIGIBILITY
- Bid only by firms qualified under ref. 241140017394. The qualified list is not public. Phase One winners (Kabbani/Alfanar; Albawani/Shibh Al-Jazira/Alghanim) are the obvious likely qualifiers (INFERENCE).
- Genset vendors will need MoD vendor approval or approval inside the contractor's submittal. Security clearance for site personnel is likely (INFERENCE).

COMPETITORS (brand via bidder; all INFERENCE unless stated)
- Alfanar (Phase One incumbent) is a large electrical manufacturer and EPC. It will buy sets from a packager, and incumbency on the Phase One power plant gives it a brand-standardisation argument. Brand unknown.
- Caterpillar via Zahid Tractor is the default rival on MoD and large-base work.
- mtu (Rolls-Royce) is likely where the Phase One plant or critical loads use high-speed 16/20V sets.
- Local packagers: Gulf Power (Alkhorayef, per its site using John Deere, Volvo, Baudouin, Deutz and also Cummins engines), plus Perkins/FG Wilson packagers.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. By 3 Oct: ask Dar AlRiyadh (consultant) for the Phase Two electrical spec and approved-vendor list. Ask whether Phase One standardised a genset brand.
2. By 6 Oct: send 60 Hz budget quotes (C2000D6/C2500D6-class paralleled sets for any central generation, plus C500D6-C1000D6 building and pumping-station standby with PowerCommand ATS and paralleling) to Kabbani/Alfanar, Albawani, Shibh Al-Jazira and Alghanim International estimating teams. Also send to any other firm confirmed as qualified.
3. Offer a locally packaged, SASO/LCGPA-compliant configuration and a multi-year O&M/parts package from the Dammam/Eastern branch (Hafr Al-Batin is about 450 km from Dammam).
4. After 20 Oct, track the lowest bidder and lock the MEP subcontractor before the vendor list is frozen.

RISKS
- Phase Two value is unclear. Construction Review cites MEED Projects valuing 'Package 2' at ~$1.36bn and 'Package 1' at ~$783m. $783m matches Phase ONE package 1, so the $1.36bn may be an earlier estimate of Phase One package 2 (awarded at ~$1bn), not the Phase Two tender.
- Power generation may be an extension of the Phase One plant already specified by Alfanar, which gives lock-in.
- The MoD restricted process gives little visibility, and deadlines on MoD tenders often slip.

SOURCES
https://guest.meed.com/saudi-arabia-tenders-next-phase-of-king-saud-air-base/ ; https://constructionreviewonline.com/king-saud-air-base-1-36-billion-phase-two-construction-tender-moves-saudi-project-forward/ ; https://en.sharikatmubasher.com/media-hub/news/21506235/egypts-petrojet-wins-160mn-contract-in-saudi-arabia?lang=en ; https://www.meed.com/saudi-arabia-evaluates-king-saud-air-base-bids (14 Jan 2025, paywalled) ; https://www.stanleyconsultants.com/solutions/planning-consulting/project/king-saud-air-base ; https://www.spa.gov.sa/1475763 ; https://www.cummins.com/generators/c2000d6

tenders.leanTxt:
WHAT IT IS
Package 14 ('Eastern A Cluster') of National Water Company's long-term operations and maintenance (LTOM) sewage programme, phase two. MEED (28 Apr 2026): 'the Eastern A Cluster (LTOM14) package covers the upgrade of six existing sewage treatment plants with a capacity expansion of 30,000 cubic metres a day (cm/d) at Al Jarodia STP. This will increase total treatment capacity from about 263,000 cubic metres a day (cm/d) to approximately 293,000 cm/d, with an estimated cost of $180m. The bid submission deadline is 30 September.' (https://guest.meed.com/nwc-tenders-next-phase-of-sewage-treatment-programme/). Al-Jarodia is in Qatif governorate (Eastern Province). The other five plant names are not published.

SCOPE CHANGE HISTORY (why sources disagree)
- Before tender, MEED (4 Mar 2026) described LTOM14 as 'the construction of 10 sewage treatment plants' with 'a total capacity of 184,440 cm/d' at $180m (https://guest.meed.com/nwc-to-tender-next-phase-of-sewage-treatment-programme/). Smart Water Magazine (29 Apr) and Global Flow Control (30 Apr) still carry the 10-plant/184,440 figure.
- The tender as issued (MEED 28 Apr, 2 Sep and 4 Sep 2026) is six existing STPs, 263,000 to 293,000 cm/d. MEED also reports NWC 'grouping some upcoming projects': LTOM13 is on hold or merged, and LTOM15 (Eastern B, 2 STPs, 152,000 cm/d) is 'cancelled and has likely been merged'. LTOM16 (Central, 14 STPs) is the next tender, 'potentially in November' (https://guest.meed.com/firms-prepare-bids-for-nwc-sewage-treatment-package-14/).

CONTRACT MODEL (from sister packages)
- LTOM is 'procured on an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) basis with a long-term operations component' (MEED 13 Mar 2026). Awards go on lowest tariff: LTOM11 went to the consortium that 'offered the lowest tariff'.
- LTOM10 signed 2 Sep 2026: 'SR1.3bn ($347m) ... The 15-year contract ... includes an initial three-year period for rehabilitation and upgrade works, followed by long-term operation and maintenance. NWC said the contract was signed with a tariff of SR0.69 ($0.18) a cubic meter.' (https://guest.meed.com/nwc-confirms-347m-sewage-treatment-plant-deal/). Expect LTOM14 to follow: roughly 3-year rehab plus O&M to year 15, with tariff-based payment (INFERENCE from LTOM10).
- Eastern Province precedent: LTOM7 Al Ahsa (Alkhorayef, SR1.7bn) had 'rehabilitation works ... in two phases within 36 months' and 'O&M ... for 15 years' (https://guest.meed.com/local-contractor-wins-al-ahsa-sewage-package/).
- Financial adviser for the whole programme: Synergy Consulting (MEED 4 Sep 2026).

SCOPE & RATINGS
- No genset schedule is public. NWC's Phase 2 RFQ (https://www.nwc.com.sa/AR/BusinessSector/VendorsRelationships/Documents/NWC%20LTOM%20Phase%202%20-%20RFQ%206.8.2024.pdf) is behind Cloudflare (403) and could not be read.
- INFERENCE: the O&M operator carries the availability and effluent-quality risk for 15 years. It must keep inlet/lift pumping, aeration blowers (partial), UV/chlorination and SCADA running through SEC outages. That means standby diesel at each STP sized for critical process load (not full aeration), typically 0.5-1.5 MW per plant for 20,000-80,000 cm/d plants. The genset split across the six plants is unknown. Some existing sets will be refurbished rather than replaced.
- 60 Hz, 400 V LV (or 13.8 kV MV at larger plants), Eastern Province coastal/humid (Qatif): expect corrosion-protected enclosures and high-ambient radiators (INFERENCE).

DATES & PROCESS
- Tendered April 2026 (restricted RFP to LTOM-qualified firms). Bid submission 30 Sep 2026, i.e. TOMORROW relative to this check (29 Sep). No extension was reported in MEED coverage up to 29 Sep.
- Evaluation: technical, then financial (tariff) opening. LTOM12 financials were opened about 12+ months after the tender, and LTOM12 is still under evaluation. So expect award in H1-H2 2027 (INFERENCE from LTOM11/12 timelines).

COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Estimated cost $180m (MEED). Tariff-based O&M revenue. Bonds and fees are not public (RFP restricted).

ELIGIBILITY
- Bidders come from the NWC LTOM Phase 2 RFQ prequalification (RFQ doc dated 6 Aug 2024 per filename). Named bidders (MEED 4 Sep 2026): Alkhorayef Water & Power Technologies, Civil Works Company, Miahona. United Water/Armada (LTOM10/11 winner) and Beijing Enterprises are NOT bidding.

COMPETITORS (brand via bidder)
- Alkhorayef Water & Power Technologies (AWPT): its sister company Gulf Power ('a proud division of Alkhorayef Group') packages 9-3,400 kVA gensets in Riyadh. Its site shows OEM partners Cummins, Deutz, John Deere, Volvo and Baudouin (https://gulfpower.com.sa/). If AWPT wins, the sets will very likely be Gulf Power packages (INFERENCE). Cummins' play is then to be the ENGINE inside the Gulf Power package, not a competing genset. AWPT is the incumbent LTOM operator in the Eastern Province (Al Ahsa LTOM7) and won three Phase 1 packages worth >SR5.53bn (MEED 12 Feb 2026).
- Civil Works Company (Al-Awael group): partnered with Suez and Veolia on Phase 1 packages. Genset brand unknown. Open to Cat (Zahid), Cummins or Perkins packagers.
- Miahona (Al Muhaidib group, listed): won the Phase 1 Hada/Arana package with Thabat. Genset brand unknown.
- Aggreko / rental firms: temporary power during rehab shutdowns (INFERENCE).

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. Today (29-30 Sep): the bid is closing, so shift from specification to post-bid positioning. Call the three bidders' procurement leads to confirm Cummins is on their vendor list. Offer a firm unit-rate letter (per-kVA supply plus 15-yr service rate card) they can use in clarifications.
2. Gulf Power: agree an engine-supply price (QSK/QSX 60 Hz engines) so Cummins wins even if AWPT takes LTOM14.
3. Civil Works Co. and Miahona: offer complete 60 Hz standby packages (C500D6-C1500D6 class) with PowerCommand ATS, remote monitoring for SCADA, and a 15-year parts and service agreement from the Dammam branch, with availability guarantees matching NWC penalties.
4. Watch the award (likely 2027), then pitch the winner within the first month of the 3-year rehab.
5. Pipeline: LTOM16 Central (14 STPs) RFP expected November 2026. Pre-position with the same three bidders now.

RISKS
- Bid closes 30 Sep, so there is little chance to influence the offer.
- AWPT has a captive packager (Gulf Power).
- Rehab may reuse existing sets, cutting new-unit volume.
- NWC has repeatedly re-scoped and merged packages.
- Award timelines run 12+ months.

tenders.leanTxt:
WHAT IT IS
The main construction package for the Ajyad residential tower, a 365 m, 84-floor residential supertall with 4 basements in Mecca's central area near the Grand Mosque. Developer: Rua Al-Haram Al-Makki Company (PIF, est. Oct 2017). The same developer is behind the King Salman Gate mixed-use scheme (12m+ sq m GFA, launched Oct 2025: https://guest.meed.com/saudi-crown-prince-launches-king-salman-gate-project/). MEED (16 Jul 2026): 'Rua Al-Haram Al-Makki has tendered the main construction package for the Ajyad residential tower, a 365-metre high-rise development in Mecca's central area, close to the grand mosque. The bid submission deadline is 30 September.' ... 'The tower rises 84 floors with four basement levels. It comprises a total of 212 units, including 82 three-bedroom apartments, 85 four-bedroom units, 29 penthouses and 16 duplex villas. The scheme has a gross floor area of 209,231 square metres (sq m) and a built-up area of 242,976 sq m. The site is currently being cleared by a demolition contractor, with the existing mat foundation and retaining walls to be handed over to the main contractor, who will build the new superstructure on the retained raft.' (https://guest.meed.com/pif-developer-tenders-365-metre-mecca-residential-tower/). Construction Week Saudi also covered the tender ('PIF Firm Seeks Bids for One of Makkah's Tallest Towers', https://constructionweeksaudi.com/projects-tenders/rua-alharam-almakki-365-metre-makkah-residential-tower-tender). That page is bot-blocked, and search snippets show no facts beyond MEED's.

PROJECT TEAM (MEED)
Marriott International (residential operator); Hanmi Global Saudi (PMC); Saudi Diyar Consultants (construction supervision); PLP Architecture (lead design consultant and construction-stage design guardian). The MEP engineer of record is not named. PLP typically works with international MEP engineers, but that is unconfirmed.

SCOPE & RATINGS
- No MEP or genset schedule is public. No bidder list is public.
- Code basis (sourced): SBC 201 §403.4 sets high-rise emergency and standby power requirements, which were significantly changed in the 2024 edition (VortexFire, https://vortexfire.com/insights/sbc-201-801-2024-edition-the-key-changes-you-need-to-know). SBC 801 §1203 covers emergency and standby power systems. Civil Defense approval, including Salamah, is mandatory. SBC 801 requires at least two fire-service access elevators in buildings over 36 m. At 365 m, the tower is far above that threshold, so standby must carry fire pumps, fire-service and occupant-evacuation lifts, smoke control and pressurisation, and emergency lighting (legal basis sourced; load list is INFERENCE based on the IBC-derived SBC).
- Brand standards (INFERENCE): Marriott-branded residences usually add standby for domestic water pumping, some HVAC and lifts beyond code minimum.
- Sizing (ESTIMATE): 242,976 sq m BUA. Code life-safety plus Marriott partial backup at roughly 25-40 W/sq m gives ~6-10 MW. That suggests 3-5 x 2,000-2,500 kWe 60 Hz sets (e.g. C2000D6 / C2500D6-class on QSK60/QSK78) in N+1 paralleled configuration with PowerCommand. A supertall may split sets between the basement and a mid-height or roof plant floor. That split drives fuel transfer, day tanks and flue design, where package engineering can differentiate (INFERENCE).
- Electrical: 60 Hz, likely 13.8 kV SEC supply with LV or MV generation (unconfirmed).

DATES & PROCESS
- Tender issued by 16 Jul 2026 (MEED). Bids due 30 Sep 2026, i.e. tomorrow relative to this check. No extension reported by MEED.
- Private-client tender run by the PMC (Hanmi Global Saudi), not on Etimad. The evaluation basis is not public.
- Genset purchase timing (INFERENCE): the main contractor or its MEP subcontractor will procure gensets 12-24 months after award, once the superstructure is well advanced. So there is a second window after award, at MEP subcontract and vendor-list stage.

COMMERCIAL / ELIGIBILITY
- Bonds, fees and eligibility are not public. PIF real-estate clients usually invite prequalified Tier-1 contractors and ask for ICV/local-content plans (general practice, unverified for this tender).
- Makkah central-area works need Makkah Municipality / Royal Commission for Makkah City and Holy Sites permits and restricted-hours logistics (INFERENCE).

COMPETITORS
- Bidders are not public. Likely Tier-1 high-rise bidders (INFERENCE): Saudi Binladin Group (dominant in the Haram area; also completing Jeddah Tower per MEED https://guest.meed.com/saudi-binladin-group-makes-a-comeback/), China State Construction (CSCEC), El Seif Engineering, Nesma & Partners, and Al-Rashid/other Makkah-focused contractors.
- Genset competitors: Caterpillar via Zahid Tractor (strong in Western Region hotel towers), mtu via packagers, Kohler-SDMO, Perkins/FG Wilson packagers. Brands at nearby Haram-area towers were not found in public sources.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. By 1 Oct: email Hanmi Global Saudi (PMC) and Saudi Diyar (supervision) asking whether the specification carries an approved-vendor list for generators. Request that Cummins (locally packaged, SASO-certified) is listed. Offer a technical submittal pack for 60 Hz 2-2.5 MW sets with NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance.
2. By 3 Oct: confirm the bidder list through Hanmi or market contacts. Send budget prices and fuel-system/flue concepts to each bidder's MEP arm for use in post-bid clarifications.
3. After award (likely Q1-Q2 2027): pursue the MEP subcontractor before the genset submittal. Pitch high-rise references, 24/7 Western Region service (Jeddah/Makkah) and a long-term service agreement. Marriott operations value guaranteed response times during Hajj and Ramadan peaks.
4. Use this tower as the entry to Rua Al-Haram's much larger King Salman Gate programme. Register Cummins with Rua's procurement.

RISKS
- Bid closes 30 Sep, so the pre-bid influence window is gone.
- Genset scope is inferred, not published.
- PIF real-estate tenders are often extended or re-packaged, and the award could slip.
- The MEP engineer may specify a brand already standardised on nearby Rua/Haram assets.

SOURCES
https://guest.meed.com/pif-developer-tenders-365-metre-mecca-residential-tower/ ; https://constructionweeksaudi.com/projects-tenders/rua-alharam-almakki-365-metre-makkah-residential-tower-tender ; https://guest.meed.com/saudi-crown-prince-launches-king-salman-gate-project/ ; https://vortexfire.com/insights/sbc-201-801-2024-edition-the-key-changes-you-need-to-know ; https://sbc.gov.sa/ar/BC/Documents/tableofcontent2024/SBC%20801/SBC801_CR_241224-FA.pdf ; https://guest.meed.com/saudi-binladin-group-makes-a-comeback/

tenders.leanTxt:
WHAT IT IS
Construction of the Souq areas at the centre of the Expo 2030 Riyadh site (6 sq km, north Riyadh, next to King Salman International airport). Client: Expo 2030 Riyadh Company (ERC, 100% PIF, launched June 2025). MEED (8 Sep 2026): 'The tender was floated on 30 July, with a submission deadline of 9 October. The Souq areas are divided into five distinct precincts, with a total development area of about 300,000 square metres (sq m). The scope includes the five precincts and their associated vertical elements, infrastructure and public realm works.' Precincts: 1 The Icon 41,417 sq m; 2 Place & Planet 62,306 sq m; 3 Culture of Wisdom 67,112 sq m; 4 Kingdom of Saudi Arabia 45,967 sq m; 5 Adaptation & Innovation 82,358 sq m. The package 'will interface with three public parks' and 'tie into the Natural Corridor, including bridges'. It will house 'rented and partnership pavilions, alongside a range of food and beverage, retail and visitor-experience offerings' (https://guest.meed.com/riyadh-tenders-expo-2030-souq-areas-package/).

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS PACKAGE (sourced)
The signature assets in the same precincts are procured separately:
- The Icon: 66 m tall, BUA ~16,279 sq m, EOI 20-23 Jul 2026 (https://guest.meed.com/riyadh-seeks-contractors-for-expo-icon-asset/).
- Early works and substructure for the Icon, convention centre and Culture of Wisdom, Place & Planet and Adaptation & Innovation pavilions: EOIs 23 Jul 2026 (https://guest.meed.com/contractors-submit-riyadh-expo-substructure-interest/).
- KSA pavilion: tendered 19 May, bids 26 Aug 2026 (https://guest.meed.com/expo-riyadh-tenders-saudi-arabia-pavilion/).
- Convention centre D&B: EOI 14 Sep 2026, award by end-2026 (https://guest.meed.com/firms-submit-expo-2030-convention-centre-interest/).
- Place & Planet pavilion lead design: AtkinsRealis (https://guest.meed.com/atkinsrealis-wins-expo-2030-riyadh-design-deal/).
So the Souq package is the surrounding mixed-use, low-rise buildings (rented and partnership pavilions, F&B, retail), plus public realm and precinct infrastructure. This reading is INFERENCE from the separate procurement.

POWER CONTEXT (sourced)
MEED (14 Jul 2026): 'an agreement for permanent supply has been signed. Design and procurement of the main substation and primary power infrastructure are under way ... full permanent power – at a capacity of 400MW – targeted approximately 18 months ahead of the event. An initial 25MW supply to power site operations and support testing and commissioning is already installed' (https://guest.meed.com/expo-2030-riyadh-construction-gathers-pace/). Alfanar signed with National Grid SA for a 132/13.8 kV substation for the Expo network (Transformer Magazine, 24 Aug 2026, https://transformer-magazine.com/news/alfanar-wins-expo-2030-riyadh-substation-contract/). Nesma builds the primary utility corridor (HV power, water, sewerage, comms). Al-Yamama builds the secondary networks into the central event area.
Implication (INFERENCE): the grid is the prime source, so Souq gensets are STANDBY (life safety, F&B cold chain, security/ICT, crowd-safety systems) and not prime. The Expo event (1 Oct 2030 to 31 Mar 2031, 40m+ visits) will also need event-overlay temporary power, procured separately, probably around 2029-30.

SCOPE & RATINGS
- No genset schedule is public. ESTIMATE: ~300,000 sq m of development area. Assuming ~60-70% is built floor area in low-rise F&B/retail/pavilion buildings with 10-20 W/sq m life-safety plus critical standby gives ~2-4 MW permanent standby (distributed, e.g. 8-20 sets of 150-500 kWe with ATS). Add cold-chain/F&B and security backup up to ~6 MW. This is lower than the previous record's 4-10 MW because the signature pavilions are excluded.
- 60 Hz, 400 V (13.8 kV distribution from the Alfanar/NGSA substation).
- Sustainability (INFERENCE): Expo legacy design and BIE sustainability goals may push HVO-capable or Stage/Tier-compliant sets, or battery hybrid for events. Ask ERC's design leads.

DATES & PROCESS
- Floated 30 Jul 2026. Bid deadline 9 Oct 2026 (no extension reported as of 29 Sep). Private ERC procurement (not Etimad). ERC uses short EOI windows (1-3 days on the Icon and convention centre) and awards fast, since everything must be complete by early 2030.
- Genset procurement window (INFERENCE): MEP subcontract award Q1-Q2 2027, equipment submittals and orders 2027-28.

COMMERCIAL / ELIGIBILITY
- Not public. ERC runs EOI/prequalification rounds before each tender, so bidders are pre-screened. Expect PIF-standard local-content (LCGPA/ICV) requirements (INFERENCE).

COMPETITORS
- Bidders are not published. Likely pool (INFERENCE) from firms active at the Expo site and on large Riyadh vertical work: Nesma & Partners, Al-Yamama, El Seif, Almabani, China State Construction, China Harbour, and Binyah (earthworks).
- Genset rivals: Caterpillar via Zahid Tractor, mtu packagers, Perkins/FG Wilson packagers, Gulf Power and other local packagers. For the event overlay: Aggreko and Altaaqa (temporary power).

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. By 3 Oct: ask ERC procurement and each precinct's design lead (AtkinsRealis for Place & Planet; others via ERC) for the Souq MEP spec and vendor list. Offer an Expo-wide standby standard (one brand across all ERC assets simplifies O&M through the 6-month event).
2. By 7 Oct: send budget quotes for distributed 150-500 kWe 60 Hz standby sets plus PowerCommand ATS and remote monitoring to the MEP estimators of Nesma, Al-Yamama, El Seif, Almabani and China State.
3. Q4 2026: open a separate channel for the Expo EVENT-power framework with ERC's operations team. Offer the Cummins Arabia rental fleet plus HVO-ready sets, positioned against Aggreko and Altaaqa.
4. Treat the Souq as the anchor for an ERC-wide framework covering the Icon, convention centre, KSA pavilion and hotel.

RISKS
- Genset scope is inferred.
- Distributed small sets are price-driven, which suits local packagers.
- ERC may centralise standby or skip diesel in favour of grid redundancy plus BESS on sustainability grounds.
- The bidder list is unknown.

tenders.leanTxt:
WHAT IT IS
A design-and-build contract for Saudi Royal Aviation's (SRA, the government-owned royal flight operator, ICAO code SRA) new aviation complex inside the King Salman International Airport (KSIA) masterplan in Riyadh. MEED (17 Sep 2026): 'Contractors are preparing to submit proposals by 8 October for an estimated SR3bn ($817m) contract ... Government-owned aviation organisation Saudi Royal Aviation (SRA) tendered the contract in August. Phase one of the programme comprised the concept design stage, which has been completed by the design consultant. SRA is now seeking to deliver the second phase, which covers design development, detailed design, procurement, construction, testing, commissioning and close-out of the works. The scope covers 30 landside buildings, including 16 screening areas and gates, in addition to 15 airside buildings, including four gates. The assets include maintenance hangars; workshops; office and administrative buildings – including interior fit-out; warehouses; storage, security and catering facilities; aprons and access roads; and site utilities and civil works. King Salman International airport will provide primary utilities to designated tie-in points, with the contractor taking responsibility from there. While it is within King Salman International airport's boundaries, the site is classified as landside and is a greenfield development. The contractor must therefore meet airport security, safety and access requirements in addition to SRA's own clearance processes.' (https://guest.meed.com/contractors-prepare-riyadh-airport-aviation-complex-bids/). The concept-design consultant is not named publicly.

SISTER PACKAGES AT KSIA (who is on site; sourced)
- KSIADC (PIF) masterplan team: Foster + Partners (masterplan), Jacobs (detailed masterplan and runways), Mace (construction consultancy), Nera (airspace) (SPA/Argaam, https://www.argaam.com/ar/article/articledetail/id/1749538). Bechtel is delivery partner for the terminals (MEED May 2025).
- Terminal 6 enabling and substructure: CCECC + Mofarreh AlHarbi & Partners JV (https://guest.meed.com/contractors-win-king-salman-airport-package-deal/).
- T6 apron/taxiway ECI shortlist (up to ~$800m): Nesma & Partners/Limak/Samsung C&T/Alayuni; Saudi Arabian Trading & Construction Co/Top International Engineering; Al-Rashid Trading & Contracting/IC Ictas (https://guest.meed.com/king-salman-airport-selects-three-firms-for-apron-eci/).
- KSIA STP (SR700m): Safari Company selected, with Jacobs as consultant. The seven local bidders included Saudi Services for Electro-Mechanic Works (SSEM) and Nesma Water & Energy (https://guest.meed.com/contractor-selected-for-riyadh-airport-sewage-plant/).
These firms are the natural bidder pool for the SRA complex (INFERENCE). MEED has not named the SRA bidders.

SCOPE & RATINGS
- No genset schedule is public. The MEED text confirms 'site utilities' are in the contractor's scope downstream of KSIA tie-ins. Primary power therefore comes from the KSIA grid, and gensets are standby (INFERENCE).
- Standby drivers (INFERENCE based on industry norms, not SRA documents):
  - Hangars: NFPA 409 foam fire-suppression pumps need reliable power. Fire pumps are often diesel-driven or on generator.
  - 16+4 screening areas and gates: security screening and access control on UPS plus generator.
  - Catering: cold-chain standby.
  - Ops/IT/security buildings: Tier-style N+1 standby.
  - Apron/400 Hz GPU and AGL: airside lighting is usually on KSIA's airfield secondary-power system, which is outside this scope.
- Sizing (ESTIMATE): 45 buildings plus hangars. Critical standby ~6-10 MW, e.g. a central plant of 3-5 x 2,000 kWe 60 Hz sets (C2000D6-class, N+1, PowerCommand paralleling) plus 8-15 distributed building sets of 300-1,000 kWe with ATS. For a royal and VIP operator, full-facility backup with N+1 is plausible, which pushes toward the upper end.
- 60 Hz, 13.8 kV/400 V. Riyadh ambient ~50 C, so derating and high-ambient cooling apply.

DATES & PROCESS
- Tendered August 2026 by SRA directly (not on KSIADC's PIF platform). Proposals due 8 Oct 2026 (no extension reported as of 29 Sep).
- Security: the contractor must meet KSIA and SRA clearance processes. Vendor and site-staff vetting is likely.
- Genset procurement (INFERENCE): the design-build contractor finalises detailed design in 2027, then submits and orders equipment in 2027-28. The equipment-selection window stays open after the bid, because design development is in scope.

COMMERCIAL / ELIGIBILITY
- Estimated SR3bn ($817m) (MEED). Bonds, fees and local-content rules are not public. As a government entity, SRA is likely subject to the Government Tenders & Procurement Law and LCGPA local-content preference (INFERENCE; the procurement route is not confirmed as Etimad).

COMPETITORS
- Genset rivals (INFERENCE): Caterpillar via Zahid Tractor (strong in Riyadh government/aviation), mtu via packagers (common in airport central plants), Kohler-SDMO, Perkins/FG Wilson packagers, and Gulf Power and local packagers on smaller building sets.
- Via bidders (INFERENCE): Nesma & Partners, Al-Rashid, SAPAC (Saudi Arabian Trading & Construction), Mofarreh AlHarbi, El Seif and Almabani are likely bidders. Each uses its own MEP arm or an MEP subcontractor (e.g. SSEM, a KSIA STP bidder). Their prior genset-brand preferences are not publicly documented.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. By 2 Oct: ask SRA's procurement or the concept-design consultant for the electrical basis of design. Push for an N+1 paralleled standby plant with PowerCommand and remote monitoring, since a design-build spec is performance-based and the contractor picks the brand.
2. By 6 Oct: send 60 Hz budget quotes (central C2000D6/C2500D6-class plant plus C500D6-C1000D6 building sets and ATS, 10-year LTSA) to the estimating/MEP teams of Nesma & Partners, Al-Rashid, SAPAC, Mofarreh AlHarbi, El Seif and Almabani.
3. After award (likely Q1 2027): engage the design-build contractor's MEP designer during design development. Offer aviation references and a Riyadh 24/7 service SLA suited to a VIP flight operation. Line up SRA security vetting of Cummins service staff early.
4. Use SRA as a reference into KSIADC's own packages (T6 central utilities, STP pumping stations via Safari).

RISKS
- Genset scope is inferred.
- KSIA may supply redundant grid feeds and reduce the genset scope.
- The security-vetting burden may favour incumbent vendors.
- The bidder list is unknown, and the deadline may slip.

SOURCES
https://guest.meed.com/contractors-prepare-riyadh-airport-aviation-complex-bids/ ; https://guest.meed.com/contractors-win-king-salman-airport-package-deal/ ; https://guest.meed.com/king-salman-airport-selects-three-firms-for-apron-eci/ ; https://guest.meed.com/firms-submit-king-salman-airport-project-prequalifications/ ; https://guest.meed.com/contractor-selected-for-riyadh-airport-sewage-plant/ ; https://www.argaam.com/ar/article/articledetail/id/1749538 ; https://www.spa.gov.sa/N2157633

tenders.leanTxt:
WHAT IT IS
Kuwait Gulf Oil Company (KGOC, a KPC subsidiary that manages Kuwait's share of the Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral/Divided Zone) has tendered, as ONE EPC package, the onshore processing facility (OPF) next to KIPIC's Al-Zour refinery that will receive Kuwait's share of gas and condensate from the offshore Dorra field. MEED (25 Aug 2026): "State-owned Kuwait Gulf Oil Company (KGOC) has issued the tender for the development of an onshore gas plant next to the Al-Zour refinery ... The project budget is estimated at $3.3bn, and the bid deadline is 29 December ... The tender was issued on 23 August." MEED says it would be "the country's biggest oil and gas sector contract award in more than a decade" (14 Sep 2026). Surplus gas goes to KOC for possible injection into its oil fields.

SCOPE & RATINGS
Plant: up to 632 MMcfd gas; condensate reported as 60,000 b/d (MEED Aug/Sep 2026) and 88,900 b/d (MEED 10 Aug 2026 and earlier) - sources disagree. Licensed units: Honeywell UOP (acid gas removal) and Shell Catalysts & Technologies (sulphur recovery). Plot: 700,000 m2 per MEED; 683,715 m2 per the Kuwait Municipal Council technical committee approval (Argaam, 3 Dec 2025). Site may need shoring, backfilling and dewatering; site preparation already awarded to local Ahmadiah Contracting & Trading (MEED 10 Aug 2026).
Genset / engine scope: NOT itemised in any public source for the KGOC OPF. No source gives EDG, black-start or fire-water pump engine sizes or counts. Strongest proxy (proven, but a DIFFERENT contract): the sister KJO Dorra onshore package 3 (Tecnicas Reunidas, about $1.65bn, LOI Aug 2026) lists under Utilities: "Diesel storage and distribution system ... Fire water system Emergency diesel generator Sewage treatment" and includes a "Beach valve substation at the planned onshore processing facility next to the Al-Zour refinery" (MEED 18 Aug 2026). INFERENCE: the KGOC OPF, a larger sour-gas plant with a sulphur recovery unit, will carry the same utilities set: emergency diesel generators (safe shutdown, UPS/charger back-up, control/operator buildings), diesel fire-water pump drivers (NFPA 20 type) and possibly black-start or essential-services sets if the plant has its own gas-turbine generation. Whether main power comes from the MEW grid / Al-Zour complex or on-site GTGs is not public.
Standards (INFERENCE, not confirmed for KGOC): KPC-group plants usually apply KOC/KNPC standards. Found: "KOC-E-007 - KOC Standard for Generator Sets" (58-page standard covering generators, diesel engines, batteries, control panels, load banks and testing; Scribd copy), KOC-E-003 (generator buildings, day-tank placement per hazardous-area classification), KOC-E-006 (load transfer / automatic start of standby generators), KOC-E-011 (UPS). KGOC may issue its own or FEED-contractor (Technip Energies) specs; confirm in the ITB electrical specification.

DATES & PROCESS
- Jul 2025: early contractor engagement; FEED by Technip Energies (completed).
- 3 Dec 2025: Kuwait Municipal Council technical committee allocates the Al-Zour site to KPC for the OPF (Argaam).
- 10 Feb 2026: last pre-tender contractor meeting in Kuwait (earlier ones at Technip Energies' Abu Dhabi office).
- Apr 2026: tender put on hold due to US/Israel-Iran war; resumed.
- 23 Aug 2026: ITB issued.
- Contractors' meeting: moved from 14 Sep 2026 to 14 Oct 2026. MEED (14 Sep 2026, open guest page): "The meeting with contractors is now scheduled for 14 October 2026. Previously, it was scheduled to take place on 14 September. Sources said contractors have not been told why the meeting date was pushed back."
- Bid deadline: 29 Dec 2026 (unchanged).
- Fast-track: CAPT (Central Agency for Public Tenders) is NOT involved - "the tender process is using a fast-track model, which means that Kuwait's Central Agency for Public Tenders (Capt) will not be involved".
- INFERENCE: award realistically mid/late 2027 (KPC bid evaluation plus likely extensions; KJO's Dorra offshore bids took about 12 months from ITB to LOI). Genset/fire-pump engine vendor enquiries from EPC bidders: Oct-Dec 2026 for budget quotes; firm purchase orders 6-18 months after award (2028).

COMMERCIAL TERMS
Not public: bid bond, performance bond, document fee, payment terms, ICV/local-content rules. Value: about $3.3bn; MEED (Dec 2025) reported KGOC expected more than KD1bn ($3.3bn), possibly up to KD1.2bn ($3.9bn), up from an earlier KD850m budget, after scope changes; still intended as a single package.

ELIGIBILITY
Main bidders: selective, via KGOC's early-engagement list (ICB per TendersOnTime). For Cummins as an equipment maker: KPC group runs a central approved-manufacturer system. KLEEV (a listed manufacturer) describes approval by "The Central Prequalification Team of Kuwait Petroleum Corporation and subsidiaries", covering KOC, KNPC, KIPIC, KUFPEC, KOTC, PIC, KGOC, via registration on the KTendering portal (ktendering.com.kw), review of products/processes and factory verification. Whether Cummins gensets/fire-pump engines are on the current KPC/KGOC manufacturer list could NOT be verified (list not public); this is the first thing to check.

COMPETITORS
Main EPC bidders (contractors that attended pre-tender meetings, MEED 23 Feb / 25 Aug / 14 Sep 2026): Samsung E&A, Larsen & Toubro, Tecnicas Reunidas, Saipem, Hyundai E&C, Hyundai Engineering, JGC. Genset/engine competitors (inferred): Caterpillar via Al-Bahar (strong Kuwait oil & gas base), mtu (Rolls-Royce Power Systems), Wartsila/MAN if gas-engine or large essential-power sets, Perkins/FG Wilson and other packagers used by Korean/Indian EPCs, Aggreko for construction rental.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. Before 14 Oct 2026: confirm Cummins (engines, gensets, fire-pump engines) status on the KPC central manufacturer list via KTendering; if missing, start registration now (factory verification takes months).
2. Oct-Dec 2026: send budget offers (EDG sets, fire-water pump engines, PowerCommand paralleling, rental construction power) to the electrical/procurement leads of all seven bidders so Cummins is named in their vendor lists; Technip Energies (FEED) specs set the baseline.
3. Push Cummins Kuwait (subsidiary of Cummins Arabia, launched 2021) as the in-country service base - KPC bid evaluations weight local after-sales support.
4. Parallel, nearer-term: Tecnicas Reunidas is now executing KJO Dorra onshore package 3 ($1.65bn), which explicitly includes an emergency diesel generator and fire water system - approach TR procurement now; a TR win also helps if TR takes the KGOC OPF.
5. INFERENCE: Korean EPCs (Samsung E&A, Hyundai) often buy packaged sets from Korean packagers - pitch Cummins engines to those packagers too.

RISKS
- Iran disputes the field ("Arash"); the tender was already put on hold once (Apr 2026); security risk to offshore facilities could delay or re-scope.
- Contractor meeting already slipped once; bid deadline extensions are likely (inference).
- Genset scope may be small if the plant is grid-fed and EDGs are only for safe shutdown.
- Approved-manufacturer gate: if Cummins is not on the KPC list, EPCs cannot price it.
- Condensate capacity and scope still reported inconsistently, suggesting scope may still shift.

SOURCES
MEED guest pages (full text via WordPress API): 14 Sep 2026 contractor meeting postponed; 25 Aug 2026 tender issued; 23 Feb 2026 seven companies; 16 Apr 2026 on hold; 4 Dec 2025 value; 9 Oct 2025 fast-track; 23 Jul 2025 early engagement; 10 Aug 2026 site preparation; 18 Aug 2026 KJO package awards and package 3 utilities list. Argaam 3 Dec 2025 (site allocation). Attaqa 11 Sep 2026 (KJO PMC retender; bidders Fluor, KBR, Kent, Tecnicas Reunidas, Wood, Worley). Scribd KOC-E-007. KLEEV page on KPC approved manufacturers. Engineering News / Zawya on Cummins Kuwait launch.

tenders.leanTxt:
WHAT IT IS
Prequalification (RFQ) for the single design-and-build main contract of Dubai Metro's Gold Line (Metro Line 4), run by Dubai's Roads & Transport Authority (RTA). MEED (7 Sep 2026): "Dubai's Roads & Transport Authority (RTA) has set a deadline of 9 October for contractors to submit their prequalification statements for a contract to build the new Gold Line ... The previous deadline was 7 September." Cost about AED34bn ($9.2bn); completion September 2032. Cummins does not prequalify; the genset and rental opportunity sits with the winning consortium's E&M member or MEP subcontractor.

SCOPE & RATINGS
"A fully underground line, approximately 42 km in length. 18 underground stations" plus a depot (RTA EOI notice, Railway Gazette 25 Jun 2026); scope lists "tunnelling, underground civil works, station works (architectural, structural, MEP), rail systems, roads/utilities, safety/security systems ... and depot construction". MEED: "The contractor will be responsible for the design and build of all civil works, electromechanical equipment, rolling stock and rail systems ... assist in the systems maintenance and operations during an initial three-year period." Depth up to 40 m (Khaleej Times via Wikipedia). Route Al-Ghubaiba (Bur Dubai) to Jumeirah Golf Estates via Business Bay, Meydan, Global Village, Dubailand; interchanges with Red and Green lines and Etihad Rail.
Genset scope: NOT itemised in any public source; no RTA genset standard found publicly. Best benchmark (proven, from a Caterpillar testimonial surfaced via search; the cat.com page itself returned Access Denied to direct fetch, so not re-read): for the original Dubai Metro, Cat dealer Al-Bahar "secured the turnkey project from Dubai Metro, supplying Cat generator sets" - "multiple units of Cat diesel generator sets rated between 320 kW and 1,820 kW which will be used as emergency power"; Phase 1: 10 sets (five 3512, three 3516, one C15, one C18); Phase 2: 10 sets (three 3512, five 3516, one C15, one C18). Brand used on Route 2020 (Alstom did E&M, incl. power supply) and on the Blue Line (Limak/Mapa/CRRC) was NOT found in any public source.
INFERENCE on requirement: underground stations fall under the UAE Fire & Life Safety Code (Dubai Civil Defence), which draws on NFPA; metro practice is NFPA 130 with emergency power per NFPA 110/70. Loads: tunnel and station smoke extraction, fire pumps, emergency lighting/UPS back-up, platform screen doors, OCC/depot. Some designs rely on dual DEWA 132/33 kV bulk supply points and batteries instead of per-station gensets - this decides the size of the opportunity and is set in Aecom's design.

DATES & PROCESS
- Oct 2025: Aecom selected as RTA consultant for all five stages (concept, preliminary design, tender documents, construction supervision, defects liability); Aecom bid AED628m vs Mott MacDonald AED765m, Parsons AED843m, AtkinsRealis AED1.16bn (MEED Jun/Oct 2025).
- 21-22 Apr 2026: project launched by Sheikh Mohammed.
- May 2026: EOI (MEED: notice mid-May, deadline 13 June). Railway Gazette shows an EOI notice published 25 Jun 2026 with deadline 30 Jul 2026, submissions by email to cpdepartment@rta.ae with trade licence, company profile, authorised representative's passport and track record. The two sources disagree on EOI dates.
- Jun 2026: RFQ issued, first deadline 17 Aug 2026; extended to 7 Sep, then to 9 Oct 2026.
- INFERENCE from the Blue Line precedent (MEED): Blue Line EOI Oct 2023 -> prequalified 12 Jan 2024 -> tender documents 15 Jan 2024 -> bids 6-7 Oct 2024 (after extension from 19 Jul) -> several rounds of revised prices in Nov-Dec 2024 -> award Dec 2024 (AED20.5bn to Limak/Mapa/CRRC) -> construction April 2025 -> first major subcontract (Casco signalling) Jul 2025. Applied to the Gold Line: shortlist about Dec 2026-Jan 2027, bids about Q3-Q4 2027, award about late 2027 / early 2028, E&M/MEP subcontracts and genset enquiries about 2028-2029, station fit-out and genset delivery about 2029-2031 ahead of Sep 2032 opening. Construction-rental demand starts at award (TBM launch shafts, station boxes).

COMMERCIAL TERMS
Not public at PQ stage: bid bond, performance bond, document fee, payment terms. The Blue Line precedent shows RTA runs multiple price-revision rounds and accepts alternative offers - pressure on sub-supplier pricing is high.

ELIGIBILITY
MEED (Blue Line): the RTA requires "international contractors to work in joint ventures with local partners". EOI asks for trade licence, profile, track record; no public turnover thresholds. Consortia must cover civil + E&M + rolling stock + systems.

COMPETITORS
Main bidders: NOT named publicly for the Gold Line (MEED, Arabian Post, Wikipedia checked). INFERENCE: the five Blue Line consortia are the likeliest field: Limak/Mapa/CRRC (Blue Line winner); CSCEC/Alstom (+FCC); Larsen & Toubro/Powerchina/Wade Adams/Hitachi; China Tiesiju/Arab Contractors/Binladin/CAF; CCECC/CRCC/Hyundai Rotem/Siemens; plus Acciona/Gulermak/Alstom (Route 2020 team).
Genset competitors: Caterpillar via Al-Bahar (proven incumbent on the original Dubai Metro, 20 sets); mtu (Rolls-Royce Power Systems); Perkins/FG Wilson and Chinese packagers likely favoured by Chinese-led consortia; Aggreko, Altaaqa and local fleets for construction rental.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. Now (before 9 Oct 2026 and through the shortlist): brief Aecom's E&M/electrical design team so the specification is brand-neutral and performance-based (ISO 8528 G3, NFPA 110 Level 1, PowerCommand paralleling, local service within X hours) - Aecom writes the tender documents (stage 3).
2. After the shortlist (about Q1 2027): send budget offers for station/depot/OCC standby sets and construction rental to the E&M lead of every shortlisted consortium (Alstom, Hitachi, Siemens, CRRC, CAF, Hyundai Rotem and their MEP partners).
3. Target the local MEP houses that usually take station MEP for these consortia; also target TBM/civil partners for rental power from award.
4. Use Cummins Arabia's Jebel Ali distribution and service base as a differentiator on 3-year O&M support.
5. Use the Blue Line now as a live test: find who holds its station/depot MEP and whether gensets are still unbought (Blue Line opens Sep 2029).

RISKS
- Incumbent: Cat/Al-Bahar supplied the original metro emergency sets; RTA O&M teams may prefer the installed brand.
- Chinese/Turkish-led consortia may source Chinese-packaged sets.
- Design may minimise gensets (dual DEWA feeds plus UPS), shrinking scope.
- Long timeline: genset orders unlikely before 2028; PQ deadline already extended twice.
- Regional conflict (2026) has slowed UAE construction (MEED Apr 2026).

SOURCES
MEED guest pages (full text via WordPress API): 7 Sep 2026 October deadline; 4 Sep 2026 contractors prepare PQ; 22 Jun 2026 RFQ opens; 20 May 2026 EOI; 22 Apr 2026 announcement; 6 Oct 2025 Aecom; 10 Jun 2025 consultancy bids; Blue Line 17 Jul 2024, 8 Oct 2024, 5 Dec 2024; 8 Jul 2025 Casco subcontract. Railway Gazette EOI notice 25 Jun 2026. Arabian Post 30 Jun 2026. Caterpillar testimonial 'Cat Generators Support Dubai Metro System' (text via search snippet; page blocked to direct fetch). Alstom/Railway Technology on Route 2020 E&M. Dubai Civil Defence UAE Fire & Life Safety Code page.

The contractor designs and builds all civil works, electromechanical equipment, rolling stock and rail systems, and supports systems maintenance and operations for the first three years. Completion is September 2032. WHAT IT IS
- Saudi Ministry of Health (General Directorate, 'ديوان الوزارة، الإدارة العامة للعقود والمشتريات') public tender No. 2026100101, Etimad reference 260939000305: 'إحلال وتأمين مصادر التغذية الإحتياطية الكهربائية لمستشفى الولادة والأطفال بنجران' (replace and provide the backup electrical power sources of the Maternity & Children Hospital, Najran). Published on Etimad 14 Sep 2026 (listing API field submitionDate '2026-09-14T13:18'). Status 'معتمدة' (approved/open). No award result yet (visitor award component: 'لم يتم اعلان نتائج الترسية بعد').
- It is part of a batch. The same MoH directorate published tender 2026100104 (ref 260939000299) 'إحلال وتأمين مصادر التغذية الإحتياطية لمستشفى حوطة بني تميم بالرياض' on 16 Sep 2026, with identical terms: SAR 1,000 booklet, 18 months, two envelopes, 5% final guarantee, construction classification. Bids close 18 Oct 2026 09:00, expected award 12 Jan 2027. INFERENCE: MoH is running a programme to replace standby power at older hospitals. Tender numbers 2026100102-103 were not in the saved Etimad listing, so they may be other hospitals, closed or not yet public.
- The hospital (sehaguide.com): opened 1426H (about 2005), 'a clinical capacity of 150 beds and 200 beds available', site about 62,500 m2, main building footprint 7,020 m2. It is on King Abdulaziz Road, Al-Udhaybah North, Najran, and is the region's main MoH women's and children's hospital. Web search summaries of SPA/Al-Riyadh reports mention a paediatric floor of 54 beds (29 + 25) and 99 doctors. INFERENCE: the standby plant is original 2005 equipment, now about 20 years old, which fits a like-for-like replacement.

SCOPE & RATINGS
- NOT PUBLIC. The booklet (كراسة الشروط), BOQ and drawings sit behind the Etimad supplier login. The public attachments component (GetAttachmentsViewComponenet) returns an empty 'المرفق' block to visitors. Set count, kVA, voltage, enclosure, tank and ATS scope are not known.
- Etimad classification of the work: activity 'إمدادات الكهرباء والغاز والمياه والبخار وتكييف الهواء' (electricity, gas, water, steam & A/C supply). Work types ticked are 'أعمال الإنشاء' (construction works) and 'أعمال الصيانة والتشغيل' (O&M works). The notice also states 'تشمل المنافسة على بنود توريد: لا' ('the tender includes supply items: No'). So it is set up as a works contract, and the gensets will be bought by the contractor.
- INFERENCE, rating: sizing rules of thumb for a 150-200 bed Saudi general/maternity hospital with central chillers give 2-3 standby diesel sets of about 1,000-2,000 kVA each (total about 2.5-4 MVA). They would be 60 Hz, LV 400/230 V (or legacy 380/220 V), with a synchronising panel and ATSs, a day tank per set and a bulk tank. In KSA the chillers and ICU/NICU/OT loads are usually backed up. MoH specs usually cite NFPA 99/110 (Level 1, Type 10). The code texts were not read, so treat this as an assumption to check against the BOQ. The scope may also include removal of the old sets, new cabling/ATS, O&M during the 18 months and possibly a UPS ('مصادر التغذية' is plural and can include UPS). Confirm in the booklet.

DATES & PROCESS (all from the Etimad visitor page and its components, read 29 Sep 2026)
- Booklet on sale from 14 Sep 2026. Last date for enquiries: 24/09/2026 (13/04/1448), already passed. The page also shows 'بداية إرسال الأسئلة و الاستفسارات 29/09/2026', which contradicts the deadline (Etimad data quirk). The maximum time to answer enquiries is 5 days.
- Last date for offers: 15/10/2026 (04/05/1448) 09:59 AM. Opening: 15/10/2026 10:00 AM at 'مبنى ديوان الوزارة القديم بطريق الملك عبدالعزيز (المبنى الرئيسي ـ الدور الأول) إدارة المنافسات', Riyadh. No separate examination date ('تاريخ فحص العروض: لا يوجد'). Standstill period ('فترة التوقف'): 5 days. Expected award 10/01/2027. Works/services start 17/01/2027. Contract duration 18 months, so INFERENCE: completion around July 2028.
- Submission: 'ملفين منفصلين (فني ومالي)', i.e. separate technical and financial envelopes. INFERENCE: technical evaluation comes first and price is opened only for technically compliant bids (the usual GTPL two-envelope process).

COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Booklet price: SAR 1,000.00 ('قيمة وثائق المنافسة 1000.00'). The Etimad listing API field condetionalBookletPrice shows 500. The detail page value of 1,000 is taken as authoritative.
- Initial (bid) guarantee required ('ضمان إبتدائى'), to be delivered to the opening committee, 1st floor, old MoH HQ, King Abdulaziz Rd. Its percentage is in the booklet; INFERENCE: typically 1-2% of the bid value under the Government Tenders & Procurement Law regulations. Final guarantee: 5%. Insurance is not required ('هل التأمين من متطلبات المنافسة: لا').
- Value: not published. The programme comparables change the estimate. The MoH has awarded 12 earlier 'إحلال وتأمين مصادر التغذية الإحتياطية' hospital contracts at SAR 14.8-32.0M each; the previous Najran one, King Khalid Hospital Najran (2022100172), went to Abdulrahman Saad Al-Rashid & Sons for SAR 31,999,998.90. For a 150-200 bed hospital, INFERENCE: a contract of about SAR 18-30M, with a genset/ATS/paralleling share of 25-45%, i.e. about USD 1.2-3.6M. The earlier SAR 2.5-6M / USD 0.6-1.6M estimate was too low. Full programme award table: tenders_moh_programme.json.

ELIGIBILITY
- Contractor classification required, field 'قطاع التشييد والبناء' (construction & building sector). The public page does not show the required grade or sub-activity (e.g. electrical works).
- Execution site: inside KSA, Najran region, Najran city.
- Local content mechanisms: 'القائمة الإلزامية' (mandatory list of national products) and 'تفضيل المنشآت الصغيرة والمتوسطة' (SME preference). NOT VERIFIED: whether diesel gensets are on the LCGPA mandatory list, because the LCGPA list PDF could not be downloaded here. If they are, the contractor must source a Saudi-made (locally assembled, LCGPA-listed) genset, which favours local packagers. Check lcgpa.gov.sa before quoting.
- Bidders must be Etimad-registered with valid CR, Zakat, GOSI, Chamber and Saudization certificates (standard GTPL requirements, not tender-specific).

COMPETITORS (genset brand behind the contractors)
- Programme winners (Etimad award results): the Al-Rashid group (Abdulrahman Saad Al-Rashid & Sons / Al Rashid Technology & Power) won 6 of 12, and Abdullah Abunayyan Trading (the exclusive Kohler distributor in KSA) won 4 of 12. Noor Energy and Advanced Systems Projects won 1 each. Most low bids fail the technical envelope ('غير مطابق').
- Caterpillar through Zahid Tractor (exclusive Cat dealer in KSA; Zahid also sells FG Wilson/Perkins-engined Cat brands). Zahid has the largest MoH installed base and would be the default 'approved make' in many older MoH specs.
- Saudi local packagers with Perkins, Cummins, mtu or Volvo engines, e.g. Almajd Power (its website says it packages Perkins, Cummins and mtu engines with Deep Sea controls) and Genyard Energy (Perkins 15-2,500 kVA). These score best on the mandatory list and SME preference.
- Kanoo Machinery (Perkins generator distributor in KSA, per kanoomachinery.com/ksa).
- mtu (Rolls-Royce) through its KSA distributor, and Volvo Penta packagers for the smaller sets.
- Al-Bahar is not a factor in KSA. Its Cat territory is UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain.
- Likely prime bidders (INFERENCE): electromechanical contractors from Najran, Abha and Khamis Mushait and Riyadh MEP firms with MoH maintenance experience. The booklet purchaser list is visible only to logged-in suppliers.

HOW CUMMINS WINS
1. Now (by 2 Oct): Cummins Arabia KSA buys the booklet itself (SAR 1,000) from its Etimad supplier account to get the BOQ, drawings and the approved-makes list. INFERENCE: buying a booklet does not require the construction classification; classification is checked at award. It also shows which contractors bought the booklet.
2. By 6 Oct: send a priced turnkey genset package to every booklet buyer. It should include 60 Hz QSK50/QSK60-class standby sets sized to the BOQ, PowerCommand paralleling and ATS, day and bulk tanks, acoustic canopy or room kit, delivery to Najran, commissioning, load-bank test and 18-month O&M. Use one price list for all bidders so Cummins is named in every bid.
3. If the mandatory list covers gensets, supply through a Saudi packager that holds an LCGPA local-content certificate, e.g. a Cummins-engined local package such as Almajd, and keep PowerCommand controls and genuine service.
4. Differentiate on hospital references in KSA, PowerCommand paralleling (NFPA 110 Type 10 transfer), parts availability in the south, and a fixed-price 18-month service offer aligned with the contract's O&M element.
5. After award (expected 10 Jan 2027), close the purchase order with the winning contractor within the 5-day standstill and mobilisation window.

RISKS
- Mandatory-list or local-content rules could exclude an imported Cummins package.
- Older MoH specs may name Cat/Zahid, or 'equal approved'. Get the approved-makes clause from the booklet.
- It is a works contract, so the lowest price among technically compliant bidders wins. Local packagers undercut on price.
- Time is short: 16 days to bid close and the enquiry window has shut, so specification deviations cannot be clarified.
- Hot desert site at about 1,300 m altitude (Najran). INFERENCE: the sets need derating for about 50 C ambient and altitude, which pushes the kVA per set up. Check the site conditions in the spec.

SOURCES
- Etimad visitor page and components (fetched 29 Sep 2026): https://tenders.etimad.sa/Tender/DetailsForVisitor?STenderId=RmNHa%2A%40%40%2A%2AtXevqxTsKHiDyI4Q%3D%3D ; tenders.etimad.sa/Tender/GetTenderDatesViewComponenet, GetRelationsDetailsViewComponenet, GetLocalContentDetailsViewComponenet, GetAttachmentsViewComponenet (empty for visitors), GetAwardingResultsForVisitorViewComponenet ('لم يتم اعلان نتائج الترسية بعد'). Saved: tenders/deep/najran_main.html, tenders/ksa_gov/d_1101069.txt, tenders/ksa_gov/live_all.json (submitionDate).
- Sibling tender 2026100104 (Hawtat Bani Tamim): https://tenders.etimad.sa/Tender/DetailsForVisitor?STenderId=DAxB4jUT37YE7zQ8eLl%20uw%3D%3D (saved tenders/deep/hawtat.txt).
- Hospital size: https://sehaguide.com/en/Item/9350/Maternity-and-Children's-Hospital---Najran ('a clinical capacity of 150 beds and 200 beds available'; 'approximately 62,500 square meters total, with the main building occupying 7,020 square meters'; opened 1426H). Paediatric beds and doctor count come from search-result summaries of https://www.alriyadh.com/1962965 and https://slaati.com/2022/07/16/p2073588.html (page bodies not verified).
- Competitor pages: https://www.almajd-power.com/en/ , https://genyard.com/diesel-generator-supplier-ksa/ , https://www.kanoomachinery.com/ksa/engines-power-generation/perkins-generator , https://www.albahar.com/ (Cat territory UAE/Kuwait/Qatar/Oman/Bahrain).
- Not found publicly: MoH news on this hospital's generators, past awards for its power plant, the BOQ.
